qs.q: A 10-day-old preterm infant with necrotising enterocolitis shows no clinical improvement despite maximal medical therapy, and serial blood gases demonstrate a rising base deficit and increasing lactate. What category of surgical indication has this infant met?
o: A contraindication due to high risk of short bowel syndrome
A relative indication requiring prompt surgical evaluation
A minor finding managed purely by continuing medical therapy
An absolute indication demanding emergency laparotomy
qs.e: Clinical deterioration despite maximal medical therapy and a rising lactate or base deficit are classified as relative surgical indications. Pneumoperitoneum is the only absolute indication.
